summary: Major scope failure of the all-morphism constructible pushforward statement. Four additional local errors have precise countermodels and limited impacts. Main renormalized category and Hecke equivalence not disproved.

problems.title: Arbitrary pushforward does not land in the constructible small category

locations.anchor: Proposition3.5.5(ii), f_*:Shv_gr,c(Y)->Shv_gr,c(Z) for arbitrary stack morphism
BG_m graded cohomology is a polynomial algebra
ExampleA.4.4 compact objects have finite grading support

problems.parameters: f:BG_m over algebraic closure of F_q -> pt; F=constant graded sheaf, a compact object of Shv_gr(BG_m)^ren by the definition of constructibility.
assumptions_verified: BG_m is a finite-type Artin stack with affine stabilizers
f is a morphism in Stk_k
Constant sheaf is constructible; gr preserves compactness
Target Shv_gr,c(pt)=Vect_gr,c
problems.actual_result: f_*,ren F=Lambda[beta], beta of cohomological and graded degree2. It has nonzero components in every grade2j, j>=0, and is not compact in Vect_gr. The identity of its filtered union of finite truncations cannot factor through any finite truncation.
problems.impact: The displayed universal small-category functor and its bounded weight-structure assertion are not defined on this admissible input. This damages the stated all-morphism constructible-functor conclusion, not the construction of the renormalized large category.
problems.counterevidence: The earlier large-category formulation explicitly anticipates nonconstructible pushforward. Hecke convolution uses representable proper pushforwards and is not refuted.
problems.correction: Restrict the small-category assertion to maps/objects for which pushforward preserves constructibility, e.g. the UC_* class already defined in2.8.9; otherwise formulate an appropriately justified large-category weight statement.
problems.repair_verification: Necessary restriction and explicit counterexample verified. No general unbounded weight extension is constructed or claimed.

problems.title: Right adjoint strictness requires continuity

locations.anchor: CorollaryA.4.7; preceding LemmaA.4.6 explicitly assumes continuity

problems.parameters: A=M=N=Vect over a characteristic0 field Lambda; U=directsum_{j>=0}Lambda; F=U tensor -, G=RHom(U,-).
assumptions_verified: A compactly generated rigid symmetric monoidal
M,N A-module categories
F left adjoint to G between underlying categories
F is strict A-linear and continuous
U need not be compact under the printed corollary
problems.actual_result: The right-lax module map U tensor G(Lambda)->G(U) is the finite-rank-operator inclusion U tensor U^*->End(U). Identity_U has infinite rank and is not in its image. Thus G is not strict.
problems.impact: Unqualified corollary and its invocation for arbitrary noncontinuous usual pushforwards require correction. Core enriched-Hom proofA.5 explicitly verifies continuity of its right adjoints, and renormalized pullback preserves compactness, so no failure of those checked core uses is established.
problems.correction: Require G continuous (equivalently F preserves compactness when source compactly generated), then apply LemmaA.4.6. Without it, retain laxness or restrict scalar objects to dualizable ones.
problems.repair_verification: Countermodel is analytic, not inferred from finite matrix tests. Continuity is explicitly available in the checked A.5 and renormalized uses.

problems.title: Finite base change gives Galois conjugates, not identical copies

locations.anchor: Lemma2.7.5, g^* g_* F = F^{oplus r}

assumptions_verified: Finite extension F4/F2
Finite étale base-change morphism
F constructible and pure perverse weight0
alpha and alpha^2 distinct
problems.actual_result: g^*g_*delta_alpha=delta_alpha directsum delta_(alpha^2), not delta_alpha^{oplus2}; support differs. Exact GF4 arithmetic verifies the two-point orbit.
problems.impact: The displayed formula is false, but the proof needs only F as a retract; identity conjugate supplies that retract. For the generator theorem every conjugate is also pure and geometrically simple, so the corrected finite sum remains among the generators.
problems.correction: Replace identical copies by directsum over Gal(k_m/k_n) of sigma^*F, with the analogous conjugate sum inTheorem3.2.19.
problems.repair_verification: Retraction and generator argument verified with the corrected formula; base-extension equivalence is not disproved.

problems.title: Smooth descent statement omits the covering hypothesis

locations.anchor: Proposition2.5.10, let Z_n->Y_n be a smooth morphism

problems.parameters: Y_n=Spec(k_n) disjointunion Spec(k_n), Z_n=first component, open-and-closed immersion.
assumptions_verified: Both finite-type separated schemes, hence allowed stacks
Map smooth
Map not surjective, which is not excluded in the displayed statement
problems.actual_result: Cech nerve is constant at Z_n, so totalization is Vect_gr. Pullback from Vect_gr times Vect_gr kills the nonzero sheaf on the second point and cannot be an equivalence.
problems.impact: Literal statement exceeds smooth-cover descent. Actual atlas applications use covering maps; no failure of descent for smooth surjections is shown.
problems.correction: Require a smooth surjective map, or a jointly surjective smooth covering family.
problems.repair_verification: Counterexample exact; adding cover condition matches the mixed-sheaf descent input used in the proof.

problems.title: Algebraic-integer eigenvalue index excludes Tate twists

locations.anchor: Remark2.4.6, index set for Vect_omega described as algebraic integers

problems.parameters: q2,n1,ell3 and the standard Tate object Lambda(1) onSpecF2.
assumptions_verified: ell!=characteristic
Continuous rank1 Frobenius representation
Pure integral weight-2
Frobenius eigenvalue1/2 is an ell-adic unit
problems.actual_result: 1/2 is not an algebraic integer (primitive integer minimal polynomial2X-1). Thus the stated eigenvalue-indexed target omits an allowed invertible mixed object.
problems.impact: Ancillary omega-graded variant is misstated. The main integer-weight graded category explicitly includes negative weights and Tate shifts and is not affected.
problems.correction: Use the multiplicative group of permitted nonzero Frobenius eigenvalues (with the appropriate Weil-weight and ell-adic continuity conditions), not only algebraic integers.
problems.repair_verification: Tate obstruction and inverse closure checked. The optional variant's full formalism is not independently developed.

focused_checks.reason: The primary verifier checked the exact small-category quantifier in Proposition 3.5.5(ii), the exclusive constructible setting on p.29, and the UC_* restriction already present on pp.27-29. For f:BG_m->pt, the compact constant graded sheaf maps to Lambda[beta], with nonzero components in unbounded grading degrees. Its identity cannot factor through a finite grading truncation, so the displayed small-category functor is not defined on an allowed input. The large renormalized category, and the proper/representable Hecke applications, are explicit counterevidence against a broader failure claim. Restriction to constructibility-preserving pushforward is necessary; no unbounded weight extension is certified.

The primary verifier checked Corollary A.4.7 as an adjunction of underlying categories and Lemma A.4.6's continuity hypothesis. With U an infinite direct sum, F=U tensor - is continuous and strict, but G=RHom(U,-) is not continuous. The purported module isomorphism at U and Lambda has image the finite-rank endomorphisms of U, omitting its identity. The compactness/continuity checks in the cited renormalized and A.5 uses prevent extrapolation to those core applications.

The printed identical-copy formulas on pp.23 and 35 were checked. Over F4/F2 the two roots alpha,alpha^2 of X^2+X+1 are distinct, so the pull-push of delta_alpha has two distinct supports. The Galois-conjugate direct sum supplies the identity retract, and all conjugates retain purity and geometric simplicity. Thus the local formulas fail while these particular retraction/generation arguments survive.

Proposition 2.5.10 says smooth morphism without surjectivity. Inclusion of one component of two points is admissible, with constant Cech nerve and pullback Vect_gr x Vect_gr -> Vect_gr that kills a nonzero second-component sheaf. The missing covering hypothesis is decisive. Actual smooth-cover descent is not refuted.

Remark 2.4.6 explicitly indexes by algebraic integers, while the following Tate-shift discussion allows negative weights. At q=2, ell=3, Lambda(1) has eigenvalue 1/2, an ell-adic unit of integral weight -2 but not an algebraic integer. This defeats the stated optional eigenvalue index. It does not affect the integer-weight construction, and no complete replacement formalism is asserted.
